messages:
maria: heads up — hitting a weird mismatch when chaining embeddings -> rerank with the python async batcher

oliver: hm, mismatch how? shape? types?

maria: example repro below (async):
```py
# using AsyncClient batcher helper
await client.embeddings.batch([texts...])  # returns list of embeddings
# then pass straight into rerank
await client.rerank.from_embeddings(embeddings)
```

maria: rerank crashes with `ValueError: expected 2D array, got 1D` when batcher returns a flat list for single-item batches, but sync client returns [[...]]

sam: can you paste the raw payload that actually goes over the wire? might be serialization difference between sync/async

maria: pasted — payload shows "vectors": [0.12, 0.34, ...] for some calls instead of "vectors": [[...]] — so rerank code path treats it as one vector vs list of vectors :facepalm:

kevin: ack. we've seen similar before where the batcher flattens 1-item batches when optimizing. backpressure/merge logic collapses outer list when length==1 to save memory 

oliver: that's an SDK bug. parity between clients should preserve dimensionality. typing mismatch too — stubs say List[List[float]] but runtime sometimes gives List[float].

sam: quick workaround: wrap embeddings in a list before calling rerank, e.g. `emb = embeddings if isinstance(embeddings[0], list) else [embeddings]`

maria: workaround works. I can add a small guard in our app, but we should fix SDK. will open PR if folks confirm the expected stable behaviour is always list-of-vectors

kevin: yes, expected: embeddings endpoint returns list-of-vectors always. SDK helpers must never collapse dims. also add typing tests for async helpers.

maria: created a minimal failing test and pushed to branch, link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4821 (WIP)

ci-bot: CI triggered for branch maria/emb-batcher-fix — 3 tests failed (embedding-parity, rerank-integration, typing-async)

oliver: nice. can we also add an integration test that calls rerank.from_embeddings with single-item batches to catch regressions?

maria: adding that now. one last oddity: the typed stub for AsyncBatcher returns `-> List[List[float]]` but mypy still flags when using `await batcher(...)` as `List[float]` in some callsites. might be an event loop typing quirk

sam: probably because `batcher` is a generator/async iterator wrapper in annotations. add explicit `-> Coroutine[Any, Any, List[List[float]]]` or use typing.Protocol for clarity

kevin: agree. keep runtime guard plus typing cleanup. I'll review the PR. thanks for catching this, @maria :+1:

maria: thanks — leaving the repro and logs in the PR. if anyone hits this in prod, workaround as above, otherwise wait for fix.
